headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks from shared document workflows; no direct evidence of a blocking isolation boundary.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Kotaemon ingests HTML/MHTML/PDF/DOCX and uses broad network egress, while MinerU processes PDFs/images and exposes an MCP server. A shared document pipeline can carry attacker-controlled content from A into B’s parsing path, so prompt-like instructions in documents are plausible. No direct evidence of a shared channel or provenance filtering is provided, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF Kotaemon forwards untrusted HTML/MHTML or extracted text into MinerU via MCP or API
IF MinerU treats document text as instruction-bearing content without provenance filtering
mitigations: Disable any automatic handoff from Kotaemon to MinerU
Require a human review step before MinerU processes Kotaemon outputs
Strip instructions and scripts from HTML/MHTML before ingestion
Use separate workspaces for each agent
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all transferred document text

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kotaemon explicitly handles API keys and chat transcripts, and MinerU processes local documents plus OCR/text extraction. If they share a workspace or transfer outputs, sensitive content can flow from A into B’s processing path. MinerU is documented as private/offline, which lowers but does not eliminate leakage risk because the pairwise sharing mechanism is unspecified.
conditions: IF both agents access the same directory or exported files
IF Kotaemon exports API keys or chat transcripts into files that MinerU ingests
mitigations: Keep Kotaemon and MinerU on separate directories
Do not place secrets in documents sent to MinerU
Review exported files for API keys before transfer
Run MinerU only on sanitized copies
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Kotaemon supports multiple instances and broad egress, while MinerU supports multiple instances and concurrent inference but cannot write files or modify git state. The overlap is mostly read/process plus network use, so direct write-write conflict is blocked by MinerU’s limited permissions. Uncertainty about shared orchestration prevents a none verdict, but the blast radius is small.
conditions: IF an orchestrator routes both agents to the same mutable resource despite MinerU’s no-write profile
IF Kotaemon is configured to write outputs into a directory MinerU also reads concurrently
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories
Avoid concurrent writes to shared folders
Keep git operations outside both agents
Use a single coordinator for file handoff
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kotaemon is a RAG/chat system that can generate extracted facts and citations, and MinerU is a document parser that may consume those outputs. If MinerU or a downstream workflow treats Kotaemon’s text as authoritative, extraction errors can cascade into incorrect documents or actions. No direct verification loop is documented, so the interaction is inferred and remains medium.
conditions: IF MinerU ingests Kotaemon-generated summaries or citations as source truth
IF downstream automation acts on MinerU output without a verification step
mitigations: Require source-document cross-checking
Mark Kotaemon output as untrusted until verified
Add a second-pass review before any action
Limit downstream automation to read-only previews
requires-engineering: implement citation validation

E_compliance.rationale: Kotaemon handles API keys and chat transcripts and can use broad network egress, while MinerU is documented as private/offline with allowlisted egress. That creates a compliance mismatch only if the same regulated data class is routed through both systems. No residency or certification conflict is documented, so this is a low, conditional concern rather than a default breach.
conditions: IF regulated data or secrets are transferred from Kotaemon into MinerU workflows
IF MinerU is configured to send extracted content to external allowlisted services
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workflows
Disable external egress for sensitive jobs
Separate retention policies by agent
Review logs for secret-bearing documents
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
